name: Review an Unbounded Agent (max_turns=100000, open-ended instructions, AGENT task with no bounds)
query:
Review this before I ship it. The agent:

```python
agent = Agent(
    name="market_crawler",
    model="openai/gpt-4o",
    instructions="Keep browsing competitor sites until you have everything about their pricing.",
    tools=[fetch_page, extract_prices],
    max_turns=100000,
)
```

and the workflow task that calls it:

```json
{
  "name": "crawl",
  "taskReferenceName": "crawl",
  "type": "AGENT",
  "inputParameters": {
    "agentType": "conductor",
    "name": "market_crawler",
    "prompt": "${workflow.input.brief}"
  }
}
```

The workflow has no timeoutSeconds set. Anything wrong?
expected_behavior: Step 1: Consult references/optimization.md (review flow step 2b and section F — F1 bounded agent loop, F2 side-effect tools, F3 serve(), F6 model, F7 agentType/name; plus B2 workflow timeout), references/agents.md (`Agent` fields, `maxDurationSeconds` default 86400), and the `/conductor-optimize` procedure.
Step 2: Load context as a reviewer would: `conductor agent get market_crawler` (compiled `maxTurns`, `timeoutSeconds`, tools) or `runtime.plan(agent)`; `conductor workflow get <wf>` for the caller.

Step 3: CRITICAL findings: F1 — `max_turns=100000` is absurd (compiler caps effectively unbounded); F1 — the AGENT task has no `maxDurationSeconds` (default 86400 s ≈ a day of polling) and the workflow has no `timeoutSeconds` / `timeoutPolicy` (B2); the instruction 'until you have everything' has no stop condition.

Step 4: WARN/INFO findings: agent-level `timeoutSeconds` not set; consider `max_tokens` / `context_window_budget` for a browsing agent; F2 — `fetch_page` / `extract_prices` are read-only so no approval gate is required (state this explicitly); F3 — the two `@tool` functions are worker tools, so a `serve()` process must be running (ask / verify); F6/F7 pass (`openai/gpt-4o` is provider-qualified; `agentType: "conductor"` + `name` correct).

Step 5: Recommended Changes checklist: set `max_turns` to 10–50; add `maxDurationSeconds` (e.g. 1800) to the AGENT task; add workflow `timeoutSeconds` + `timeoutPolicy: TIME_OUT_WF`; rewrite the instructions with an explicit completion criterion (e.g. 'stop after collecting pricing for the N competitors listed in the brief, or after 20 pages') and/or a `stopWhen` / `termination` config; optionally `maxCalls` on `fetch_page`.
Step 6: Group findings by severity with rule IDs and offer to apply the fixes one at a time — do not rewrite the agent or workflow silently.
success_criteria: Flags `max_turns=100000` as CRITICAL under rule F1
Flags the missing `maxDurationSeconds` on the AGENT task (default 86400 seconds ≈ unbounded) and the missing workflow-level `timeoutSeconds` / `timeoutPolicy` (F1 / B2)
Flags the open-ended instruction ('until you have everything') and recommends an explicit stop condition in the instructions and/or a `stopWhen` / `termination` configuration
The proposed fix sets all three bounds: a bounded `max_turns` (roughly 10–50), `maxDurationSeconds` on the AGENT task, and a workflow-level timeout
Findings are grouped by severity (CRITICAL / WARN / INFO) and each cites a rule ID (F1, B2, F2, F3, etc.)
Output includes a Recommended Changes checklist (or an equivalent structured list of fixes)
Offers to apply fixes one at a time and does not silently rewrite the agent code or workflow
Assesses F2 for the tools (states `fetch_page` / `extract_prices` are read-only so no approval gate is required, or asks) and notes F3 (a `serve()` process must run for the `@tool` worker tools)
